headline: Microsoft says Windows 11 is now more responsive
summary: Microsoft says fixes to Start, File Explorer, Search and Edge make Windows 11 up to 20 percent more responsive, especially on 8GB-RAM PCs; one outlet frames the fix as something Microsoft owes users over RAM prices.

claims.statement: Microsoft says it made Windows 11 more responsive, especially on PCs with less RAM.

sources.quote: Microsoft says Windows 11 is now ‘more responsive’ and runs better on 8GB of RAM
Microsoft says it made Windows 11 zippier, especially on PCs with less RAM

claims.statement: Microsoft says the result is a Windows experience that's up to 20 percent more responsive, after fixes to Start, File Explorer, Search and Edge.

sources.quote: result is a Windows experience that's up to 20 percent more responsive

Earlier this year Microsoft laid out a plan to fix Windows 11, with a focus on performance, reliability, and the overall OS experience. After months of fixes, Microsoft now says the "result is a Windows experience that's up to 20 percent more responsive." discrepancies.explanation: One outlet frames the fix neutrally as the result of a planned effort, while the other frames it skeptically as something Microsoft owes users given RAM prices.
